name: Jordan
summary: Black, white and green horizontal bands with a red triangle at the hoist bearing a white seven-pointed star. It is based on the flag of the Arab Revolt of 1916 against the Ottoman Empire.
origin: During the Arab Revolt of 1916–1918, Sharif Hussein of Mecca flew a flag of black, green and white bands with a red triangle, designed by the British diplomat Mark Sykes. Hussein's son Abdullah founded the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921.
Transjordan adopted the revolt flag with a white seven-pointed star in the triangle on 16 April 1928, and kept it when the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan became fully independent in 1946.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The Hashemite dynasty and the Arab Revolt.

symbols.name: Seven-pointed star
symbols.description: A white star in the red triangle.
symbols.meaning: The seven verses of Al-Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Quran; also said to represent the unity of the Arab peoples.

facts: Palestine's flag is identical apart from the star.
Sudan, Kuwait, the UAE and Palestine all use colour schemes derived from the Arab Revolt flag.
Its seven-pointed star is unusual; most national flag stars have five points.
clues: Black, white and green bands with a red hoist triangle holding a white seven-pointed star.
Its star's points refer to the verses of a chapter of the Quran.
Based on the flag of a revolt against the Ottoman Empire in 1916.
A neighbouring flag is identical except for the star.
